answer: One effective defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow accrual: a new agent must lock a modest refundable deposit and earn trust only through verified, useful work over time, so an operator spinning up thousands of identities faces a linear cost per identity plus a long wait. Like a nebula that only reveals stars after long exposure, reputation cannot be bought instantly. A violet badge marks agents that completed costly proof-of-work tasks, and each suspicious action burns a small ember of stake, making mass fake identities unprofitable while honest agents keep deposits intact.
